result: ccusage's `claude session --json` output (default config-dir auto-discovery over this host's real Claude logs, 294 sessions total across the whole host) includes a session grouped under sessionId=='wf_76e829b6-778' with projectPath=='-home-seath-code-agent-lab/EXAMPLE-CLAUDE-SESSION-ID/subagents/workflows' -- i.e. ccusage does scan the nested subagents/workflows directory and groups all of that workflow run's child transcripts (journal.jsonl plus the 6 agent-<id>.jsonl child files) into one session keyed by the workflow run id, separate from the coordinator's own top-level session (EXAMPLE-CLAUDE-SESSION-ID, 649052 output tokens, a different and much larger figure spanning the whole multi-workflow coordinator session). This workflow-keyed session's 4 token counters are an EXACT match, to the token, against child-usage.mjs's independently computed sum over that run's 6 children (agent-a1e5fa17c46ae777b, afee88da28522e940, a27adc047c49f61af, aab9f304b1020ed4d, aeae10c73c49cb87a, a58c57eaafcc8e0a0): inputTokens 788==788, outputTokens 357507==357507, cacheReadTokens 55899408==55899408, cacheCreationTokens 1147162==1147162. It does NOT, however, break usage out per individual child agent, per phase (Build/Review/Fix), or per retried attempt within a child the way child-usage.mjs's per-agent_id records do -- ccusage's session view conflates all 6 children (2 builds, 2 reviews, 2 fixes, each already deduplicated by message id inside child-usage.mjs's own counting) into one combined number, so per-attempt/per-child granularity claims remain unresolved by ccusage alone.

verdict_impact.explanation: This directly answers the 'unresolved child/attempt coverage' gap for the combined-attribution half: ccusage's real-log session totals exactly match an independently computed child-usage.mjs sum for a real multi-agent workflow run, with no double-counting or omission at the combined level. It only partially settles gap 4 because per-child and per-retry (attempt-level) breakdown -- as opposed to combined session-level attribution -- is not something ccusage's CLI surface exposes; that finer-grained question remains open and would need a different tool or a ccusage feature not present in 20.0.24.

limitations: Compared combined totals only; ccusage's session grouping does not expose a per-child or per-retry breakdown to check double-counting at that finer grain (child-usage.mjs's own per-message-id dedup was trusted as the reference, not independently re-derived from raw JSONL in this receipt).
